subject: [PATCH v3 3/5] fs/proc/task_mmu: read the PMD once in smaps_pmd_entry()

reviews.author: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM)
reviews.summary: Identified a potential performance improvement by reducing PMD dereferences. Suggested making the pmdval local variable const to ensure its safety.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Agreed with the patch's intent to improve performance and suggested making the pmdval local variable const.
reviews.raw_body:
On 23 Nov 2026, at 11:32, Usama Arif wrote:

> smaps_pmd_entry() dereferences the pmd pointer six times. Read it once
> into a local with pmdp_get(), the way smaps_pte_entry() already does
> with ptep_get(), so that every test sees the same value.
>
> No functional change intended.
>
> Suggested-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
> ---
>  fs/proc/task_mmu.c | 11 ++++++-----
>  1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)
>
Makes sense.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: David Hildenbrand (Arm)
reviews.summary: Recommended picking the first two patches directly and suggested resending the remaining three for Andrew's review.

2026-11-23.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the performance of the /proc/task_mmu interface by reducing unnecessary dereferences of pmd pointers in smaps_pmd_entry(). The patch introduces a local variable to store the PMD value, which is then used throughout the function. This change has no functional impact but improves code efficiency.
